en: The ritual procedure for the lamp offering (*dīpapūjāvidhi*): First, having made the formal resolve (*saṅkalpya*), one should draw either the wheel of Durgā or a lotus; likewise, one should draw wheels with four petals. Immediately thereafter, having filled the lotus with grains and rice, and having placed a lamp in its center, one should prepare five wicks. Having thus prepared the lamp for Gaṇapati—

First, having performed the purification of the ground (*bhūśuddhi*) and the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), as well as the rites of drying, flooding, and offering, the installation of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*), the placement of the *mātṛkā* letters (*mātṛkānyāsa*), and the binding of the directions (*dikbandhana*); immediately thereafter, having performed the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) for Gaṇapati upon his lotus; and immediately thereafter, having filled [the vessel] with the mantra "O Goddess, consisting of speech" (*vāṅmayi*) and opened [the eyes]; and having invoked Durgā into the lamps by means of the visualization "O Lotus of Syllables" (*varṇāmbuja*).

Having displayed the five mudrās and performed the consecration of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) according to the prescribed rite; having performed the sixteen-fold worship (*ṣoḍaśopacārapūjā*), beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*) by means of the root mantra; immediately thereafter, one should recite the *Saptaśatī*. Afterwards, having prepared incense and lamps; immediately thereafter, the food offerings (*naivedya*) and betel leaves; immediately thereafter, having offered handfuls of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) one hundred and eight times by means of the root mantra; then, having requested the goddess Durgā with five lamps: "O Goddess, remover of all suffering, destroyer of all diseases..."
"I perform circumambulation of you for the sake of accomplishing my purpose. Thus he circumambulates.

Homage to you, O Goddess of the gods; homage to you, O protectress of devotees. Thus ends the salutation.
[The section on] worship... of this. Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the lamp offering.

The five-fold worship: *vaṃ* for the self, bathing; *laṃ* for the self of earth, perfume; *am* for the self of space, flowers; *yaṃ* for the self of wind, incense; *raṃ* for the self of fire, lamp. *Am*, O Goddess born of nectar, Mistress of nectar, You who dwell in nectar, cause the nectar to flow, cause it to flow, *svāhā*. Of this great mantra of the illustrious Bālāparameśvarī, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (*ṛṣi*); *paṅkti* is the meter (*chandaḥ*); Bālāparameśvarī is the deity (*devatā*); *aiṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *sauḥ* is the power (*śakti*), and *klīṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*). [The syllables] *vā* and *gaḥ* are for the heart and other limbs; thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the heart and so forth. Meditation (*dhyāna*): She is adorned with masses of reddish rays, her space filled with light, holding a rosary and a book, and bearing gestures of protection in her hands.
May that young woman, who dwells upon the blossoming lotus of the tip of another’s hand and whose nature is eternally auspicious, reside within my heart.

The ritual application of the mantra (*mantropacāra*) is the root. one should first remember her with blood-red garments, holding a flower and a skull-cup in her hands.

*Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ śubhā*. I salute the circle of Gurus, consisting of the three Gurus beginning with Śrīnātha, Gaṇapati, the three seats (*pīṭha*), Bhairava, the Siddhas, the [five] *ka*s, the three *ka*s, the pair of feet, the lineage of forms (*mūrtikrama*), the mandala, the eight Rādhīs, the sixty-four [deities], the face, the five rows of heroes (*vīrāvalī*), together with the King of Mantras, the glorious Mālinī. I worship the Guru’s venerable sandals; I propitiate them; obeisance! I worship and propitiate the venerable sandals of the Supreme Guru; obeisance!

I worship and satisfy the sandals of the Supreme Teacher; obeisance to him. I worship and satisfy the sandals of the Higher-Lower Teacher; obeisance to him. I worship and satisfy the sandals of my own Teacher; obeisance to him. Aiṃ! Obeisance to the two Red Teachers. Obeisance to the two Red Feet. Klīṃ! Obeisance to the two White Teachers. First, one should begin with the worship of the Guru. One should meditate upon one’s own Guru within a thousand-petaled lotus. This is the procedure for meditation. Having performed the ritual sipping of water twice and having become pure, one should assume the kukkuṭāsana posture. Holding the *cinmudrā* in the hand, with the mind made solitary, [one should visualize the Guru] as one devoted to the practice of yoga, peaceful, adorned with matted hair and a crown, resembling ten million suns, and with eyes as broad as lotus petals.
With a face like the full moon, gentle, endowed with the thirty-two marks,
knowing the true essence of the meaning of all scriptures, the embodiment of truth, and a treasure-house of compassion.
Endowed with a youthful age of sixteen years, possessing a form like ten thousand Madanas,

The Lord of the gods, whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire; the Guru who pacifies the afflictions of the Blessed One and bestows fearlessness upon his devotees;
the God endowed with the power of awakening, who grants the perfection of full enlightenment.
His two feet are worshipped by the eight goddesses beginning with Aṇimā;
he destroys all sins through remembrance, bestows liberation through sight,
cures the disease of worldly existence through touch, and grants the attainment of desired goals through salutation and other such acts.
Thus, with eyes fixed on the tip of the nose, one should meditate upon the Guru in this form for a moment,

"O Kāmeśvarī, you who delight in the movement of the desires cherished by the mind."
Having accepted the leaf, strike it; grant victory, O crusher of enemies!
(3) May [this] bestow meat and fish, served by Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the other gods;
may it grant the bliss of the practice of *mudrā* and sexual union, and may it be honored as a sweet-smelling, soft, and salty [substance]. (4)

May this vessel, established by the Teacher, purified by the placement of the eightfold state (*bhāvakalā*), accompanied by the *pañcamakāra*, and offered to the Transmigrating One (*tīrtha*), protect [us]. Yaṃ ṣam sauḥ 4.

O Śiva-Śakti, whose nature consists of Īśvara, Sadāśiva, and Pure Knowledge (*śuddhavidyā*), and who is associated with Māyā—for the purpose of purifying the lotus, I thoroughly purify and offer my causal body; Svāhā!

The third vessel: having assumed the form of Rudra. Now, the fourth vessel: may [it] be the boar; may it produce the increasingly refined essence, the divine nectar (*divyāmṛta*). To the fourth vessel, which possesses the increasingly refined essence of the nectar of Soma-juice, obeisance. To the Self consisting of primordial nature (*prakṛti*), the syllable *ha*, intellect (*buddhi*), and ego (*ahaṃkāra*), together with Māyā and the nature of Puruṣa; to Śiva, whose nature is purity, obeisance. *Āṃ* ... *kṣam*. As long as life lasts, I purify and offer [this]—*svāhā*. O Lord! Now, the fifth vessel.
[This is] served by Brahmā and others through the true dharmas proclaimed extensively in all the Āgamas;
it possesses the essence arising from the eight families of the *dīptiyāga*, is secret, and is endowed with mysteries;
it bestows existence, is supreme beyond the measured [world], and is worshipped by the followers of the *jādhā* scriptures.
One should worship the fifth vessel, which is eternally composed of Brahman, as the station of Sadāśiva.

(L5) Abiding within the trikoṇa that is the root of one’s own self, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns, I offer my own nature as Śiva into the fire of consciousness, which has the form of the kuṇḍalī. (L6)
The moist one blazes, Svāhā! I worship the form of Sadāśiva, which is variegated by diverse modes of conduct and bestows bliss and other virtues.
Charming as the kingdom of Rāma, it bestows happiness and grants liberation through union (*sāyujya-mukti*);
it dispels the darkness of fear from various diseases and instantly destroys enemies.

I worship the sixth vessel (*ṣaṣṭha-pātra*), which arose from the wood of the glorious and beautiful mirror. Alas! Having produced the supreme nectar from the teeth, I, the destroyer of the other, offer it into the great fire as the very form of Śiva.
Thus, having offered the *pūrṇāhuti*, immediately after taking up the vessel, one should form the *trikhaṇḍa* mudrā and, with the two *trikhaṇḍa* mudrās, sprinkle [it] upon one’s own head.

Now follows the procedure for the meditation on the self (*ātmadhyānavidhi*). Immediately thereafter, having placed the *cinmudrā* in one’s own hand and remained [there] for a short time, [one proceeds as follows]: (l3. immediately thereafter, with the right hand... having blocked the left nostril with the ring finger and thumb... one should expel the poison through the right nostril. Having blocked the right nostril and expelled [the poison] through the left nostril, (l4.)... [one should proceed].

Having moved here and there three times, one should block both nostrils with that vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) and, having traveled through the *mūlādhāra*, *svādhiṣṭhāna*, *maṇipūraka*, *anāhata*, *viśuddhi*, and up to the *ājñā* wheel, one should meditate upon the respective deity. Homage to Gaṇeśvara! Homage to the Creator! Homage to Mukunda! Homage to Śiva! Homage, homage to the Lord who is the embodiment of the Guru! Homage, homage! Homage to the glorious Supreme Self (*paramātman*).

Having meditated upon the respective deities in their respective [cakras] in this manner, and having recited their respective mantras, one should thereafter proceed by means of the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) to the station of the *dvādaśānta*. With a one-pointed mind and hands in the *nirmudrā* gesture, one should contemplate one's own self in this way:
"Cut through the bond! Great bliss! The unfolding of great joy!
One should contemplate the state of total heat; thus one shall abide in full bliss."
O Sovereign, Your form, which has attained the nature of the Lord in the region named the Unstruck (Anāhata) that is characterized by bliss,
is being contemplated with a serene mind.
Blessed are those who pacify [the fire] with the waters of their eyes and with tears falling from their cheeks.

Having thus meditated upon the self, the preceptor should then perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), form a mental resolve through the eightfold yoga (*aṣṭāṅgayoga*), and first recite the *Śāntistava*. Then he should begin the worship. First is the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*) and the worship of the water jar (*kalaśapūjā*). Having first drawn a triangle, he should place the jar within that mandala. Having worshipped the jar with scents, flowers, and consecrated rice grains (*akṣata*), [he should perform] the [mantra of the] jar... having displayed the jar-mudrā and the cow-mudrā (*dhenumudrā*), and having displayed the conch-mudrā over the two conches.

Having filled the conch with water from the ritual jar—O Conch, you who possess the brilliance of the sun and moon!—the waters of the wombs of women are shattered along with their cravings by your Lord; O Pāñcajanya, salutations to you! (l. 9)
O best of Brahmins, by the command of Vāsudeva, Śaṅkha stands at the sacred ford of the three worlds;
therefore, one should worship Śaṅkha.

Having beheld the conch and the cow, [one should offer salutations]: Salutation to Śaṅkha; salutation to Pāñcajanya; salutation to Kamburāja; salutation to him whose radiance is equal to the full moon; salutation to the cause of the destruction of the Daityas; salutation to him who abides as the Lord of Lakṣmī and Śaṅkara; salutation to him who consists of sound; salutation to him who is filled with sound; salutation to him whose form is an unbroken circle; salutation to the bestower of non-dual knowledge; salutation to the destroyer of the darkness of ignorance.

Homage to the one whose essential nature is the syllables *oṃ*, *hrīṃ*, and *śrīṃ*. I offer all the ritual services (*upacāra*). Having filled the flask slightly with water from the conch, having sprinkled oneself, the vessels, the implements, and the substances, and having discarded the remainder, one should fill the conch again. Then, one should perform the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭha*). O Mother, having touched [the vessel] once, twice, thrice, four times, five times, twice, and four times, reciting the root mantra in sequence over the nectar.

Homage to the one whose rampart is of *puṣparāga* gems! Homage to the one whose rampart is of *padmarāga* gems! Homage to the one whose rampart is of *gomedhaka* gems! Homage to the one whose rampart is of *marataka* gems! Homage to the one whose rampart is of *māṇikya* gems! Homage to the one whose rampart is of *muktāphala* gems!
O you who produce the bliss of unbroken nectar, O essence of the nectar of immortality, O Leader, place [me] within yourself at the moment of spontaneous recollection!
In this supreme one, who is the form of nectar situated in the midst of agitation, who produces the perfected knowledge,
and who is defined as both non-existent and eternal, one should be established in immortality.
(.... Having become that which is called reality (*tatva*), possessing the form of reality, within me who am of the nature of the nectar of the *kula*, perform your union. (l8.)

Aiṃ blūṃ ḍhīṃ juṃ saḥ, O Immortal One, O Mistress of the Immortal, O Showerer of Nectar! Cause the nectar to flow, cause it to flow, svāhā! Ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ! Aiṃ, speak, speak, O Goddess of Speech! Aiṃ klīṃ klīṃ, O Piercer, O Bed-maker! Make [him] lie down! Produce great agitation, sauḥ! [Salutations to] these Mātṛkās of the Eṭā-kala, as well as the mantras beginning with the indivisible One; salutations to the water-pot of the Pramāṇikā; salutations to the Pool of Nectar-Jewels; salutations to the Pavilion of the Heart’s Support.

Having thus performed the worship of the *pīṭha*, one should invoke the Goddess, who possesses a radiance equal to ten million suns and whose form is composed of light, with the syllables *uṃ īṃ*. Then, rising from the water-pot (*kumbha*), Hanumān, the son of the Wind-god, [invoked] Āryā Kātyāyanī with devotion— the one who bestows the fruits of both attraction and subjugation.
I bow to you, who hold a sword in hand; do not strike me with fear.
With hands granting boons and fearlessness, she removes the fear of the world of her servants;
holding a trident, a conch, a discus, a mace, and a bow;
four-armed, eight-armed, or two-armed, she is the crusher of enemies.
I bow to Umā, who consists of the universe, who possesses eighteen arms, and also to the fierce Durgā with ten arms;
she who has a thousand arms and feet, a thousand faces and eyes,
and is adorned with a thousand crowns.
I bow to her who consists of the three forms: she who resides in the lotus-face of the Lotus-born, she who dwells upon the chest of Viṣṇu, and she who abides in the left side of Hara.
I bow to that manifold power of Viṣṇu’s Māyā, which is seen as the diverse capacity of all the gods beginning with Indra, and even of the luminaries beginning with the Sun.

I bow to the divine Durgā, the slayer of Madhu, the destroyer of Kaiṭabha, the crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura,
and the slayer of Śumbha and Niśumbha.
O Mother, be gracious; you who grant boons and fearlessness and destroy suffering, quickly fulfill my desire, for this is what I long for:
may the hosts of my enemies go to their destruction this very day!
Grant me vigor, extensive victory, and fame!
|| 1 || Mother, be gracious; bestow upon me that great glory which transcends the world, without regard for others. || 2 ||*
He who worships you, who bring prosperity and auspiciousness, finds nothing difficult to obtain here, nor even in the third heaven; no other does so. || 2 ||
O Mother, be gracious! O Goddess who holds a hundred million [swords], whose pair of feet is honored by the primordial gods and who bestows everything upon all—
when you, the Blessed One, are pleased even slightly, this person here becomes Bhava.
Blessed indeed is he, and he alone is worthy of being served by the worlds,
in whom the golden-hued Goddess dwelling in the lotus— who delights in the ocean of milk— takes pleasure even for a moment within the grasp of her play.
O you who are like a wish-fulfilling creeper for prosperity, even Brahmā and the other gods become blessed by receiving the mere curve of your sidelong glance.
O Mother, be gracious, you whose body is adorned with the crescent moon!
O Manonmanī, you who abide in the state of the supreme portion, you who shine forth as the agent of the dissolution, maintenance, and creation of the universe;
you whose diverse forms consist of the earth, the night, the Great Principle (mahat), and so forth—[salutations to you]. 5.
O Mother, be gracious! O royal swan who delights in frequenting the lotus-garland of the four-faced [Brahmā]’s face;
even a mute person becomes capable of eloquence upon beholding the presence of one’s own inherent power.
Even among those who consider themselves the wisest, the steadfast one is truly wise.

O Mother, be gracious! O Goddess whose power is the soul of the immortals headed by Indra, even Brahmins with beautiful eyes sporting upon the lunar spots move about as those who have taken refuge at your feet.
The lords of the earth, sinking down, waited for their opportunity. || 7 ||
Mother, be gracious! By your favor, he shall become one who has crushed the pride of the fourfold army and destroyed the hosts of his enemies;
though now wretched, he shall obtain all desires that are otherwise difficult for others to attain.
For he who has obtained [this] shall indeed long triumph together with his sons and wife. || 8 ||
Mother, be gracious toward me out of your sudden partiality;
having observed my eighteen hardships and having set aside others, [act for me],
for otherwise there is no refuge in this world for those whose sorrows have not been dispelled.
O Mother, whose lotus feet are being served by the lords of sages—
be gracious! Why do you so suddenly disregard your child, whose ears are reddened by the flow of tears?

"O Mother Bhavānī, be gracious and hasten with compassion! For when the infant clings to your lap and you grant him the initiation of your breast-milk, he indeed attains happiness. || 10 || (l8. "Mother, be gracious! she said with haste.
If you know this dart of the heart, which is as difficult to endure as a potent poison,
then how could you, O Lady, not become the refuge of the worlds for a long time— [the worlds] who are tormented by the heat of worldly existence? 11.
"Mother, be gracious to me; O Goddess, wife of Śakra, may you yourself purify my ritual action this very day.
What is this delay? Let him come forth from his state of exhaustion."
And what is this [world] covered by the removal of misery? It is completed.
O Mother, you are pleased; you, Bhavānī, are the very personification of servitude and obedience, and you are the visible goal here in this world.
Fashioning this vessel of compassion, he has created [him] to be blessed and honored by all people. (13)
Mother, be gracious; let this be established and performed by you—this forest-dwelling for the destruction of the host of the enemies of the gods.
Through this, may there be clarity of mind for this one whose eyes are clouded.
When this world is without another protector in every respect,
O Mother, be gracious with a mind swift to show favor toward me, and with an abundance of compassion, O Lord of the Body.
Beholding me with a gaze cool as nectar, quickly grant [me] that which has been long delayed by those two who have caused such great distress. 15.
Mother, be gracious; what is the use of this delay? There is great haste in this matter, for it does not admit of waiting.
For that portion of my destiny which here [in this world] restrains the fear of the realm of the gods—
O Daughter of the Mountain, everything is entirely yours, dependent upon you in every respect.
O Mother Caṇḍikā, be gracious toward me with your supreme concentration; you are the one who is exclusively devoted, faultless, and noble.
O you who are filled with the great abundance of the perfection of good fortune!

Then spoke Suprabhā, together with Sakālī, who possessed the luster of a dark rain-cloud.
And she threatened Hanumān and the ocean with her roars.
"Welcome, Hanumān! I am now exceedingly pleased.
Therefore, O gentle one, my departure with those two has been long desired by me. I am especially gratified by your hymn of praise, which bestows what is wished for."
Those who praise me are fond of hymns and grant the fulfillment of desires. That man who recites this *kūṭa-stotra* with devotion shall, through my grace,
attain all forms of prosperity.
Whoever recites this hymn, I grant him my constant vision;
truly, I remain present before him, O Vasupradā, just as I have promised.
Whoever, knowing its meaning, should recite this, for him prosperity shall be unshakable;
and by my grace, it shall bestow boons upon his lineage as long as the earth endures.
May this hymn, which I constantly recite before me,
shine forth when joined with my kinsmen, just as you do.
A person of superior intelligence who recites this great hymn with devotion shall become a kinsman and a friend to the world, and shall be victorious everywhere.
Whoever should recite this hymn even once, whether a being or a god,
whatever desire they may wish for, that they shall obtain without doubt.
By the grace of Rāghava, all success shall be yours.
Nothing need be given by me; thus, I grant you your desired wish.
Hariḥ Om. May there be auspiciousness. Salutations to the venerable Gurus. Salutations to the illustrious Mahādurgā.
Jāmbavān, the lord of monkeys, approached the supreme Lord Śrīkaṇṭha, the cause of all perfected beings and the ruler of gods;
Hanumān said: "Salutations to you, O Rudra, husband of Gaurī; salutations to you, whose bow is the mountain."

Purifying yourself, you have taken hold of the gods; as the purifier, you have flowed toward the fire. You have struck down the demons and shattered them.
